'''David Darom''' ({{langx|he| דוד דרום}}; born 1943 in [[Bombay]], [[India]], died 28 April 2021 in [[Jerusalem]], [[Israel]]), was an Israeli [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] and [[nature photography|nature photographer]].  Until 2007, he was head of the Department of Scientific Photography at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref>David Engelberg et al, Multicellular Stalk-Like Structures in ''Saccharomyces cerevisiae'', JOURNAL OF BACTERIOLOGY, Vol. 180, No. 15, Aug. 1998, p. 3992–3996</ref>

==Biography==
David Darom was born in [[Mumbai|Bombay]], India. His family immigrated to Israel in 1949 and settled in [[Jerusalem]].<ref name="GolaniÖztürk2006"/> In 1972, he received a [[PhD]] in [[Marine biology|Marine Biology]].<ref name="GolaniÖztürk2006"/>

==Nature photography career==
Darom photographed the wildlife and wild flowers of Israel,<ref>Smilanski Y. (1996) "Let There Be Flowers" Special Weekend Edition of "Globes" (15 November), pages 12–13 (Hebrew).</ref> with special attention to the documentation of the [[List of plants in the Bible|Plants of the Bible]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://andthoushaltread.com/index.php?main_page=product_info&cPath=3&products_id=2585 |title=Beautiful Plants of the Bible &#91;9789652800671&#93; - $12.99 : And Thou Shalt Read!, Choosy Books for Chosen People |access-date=25 December 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110707141943/http://andthoushaltread.com/index.php?main_page=product_info&cPath=3&products_id=2585 |archive-date=7 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Underwater he photographed hundreds of [[fish]] species as well as marine [[invertebrates]] from the [[Red Sea]]<ref>Kesten Y. (1971) "Silence in a Thousand Colors". Ha’aretz Weekly Magazine (4 May), Cover and pages 16–17 (Hebrew).</ref><ref>Aditor’s Choice (1976) "RED SEA WONDERS" The Jerusalem POST Weekend Magazine (27 August), Cover & pages 10–11.</ref><ref>Schrag C. (1987) "FISH-EYE Lens" The Jerusalem POST Weekend Magazine (7 April), Cover & pages 10–11&15.</ref><ref>Brauner D. (1994) "Underwater Challenges for the Photographer", The Jerusalem POST (1 May)</ref> and the [[Mediterranean Sea]].<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://www.siamb.org.il/uploads/59_2_Book%20review.pdf | title=Fishes of the Eastern Mediterranean | access-date=25 December 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151126045238/http://siamb.org.il/uploads/59_2_Book%20review.pdf | archive-date=26 November 2015 | url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2001, ''[[Upeneus]] davidaromi'', a species of [[goatfish]] found in the Red Sea, was named in his honour.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Golani | first1 = D. | doi = 10.1560/TCQ5-030G-UCGV-HBFY | title = Upeneus Davidaromi, A New Deep Water Goatfish (Osteichthyes, Mullidae) from the Red Sea | journal = Israel Journal of Zoology | volume = 47 | pages = 111–121 | year = 2001 | issue = 2 | doi-broken-date = 1 July 2025 }}</ref>

== Knife collecting ==
Darom was an avid [[knife collecting|collector]] of handmade (Custom) art knives.  In 2002 he published a series of large format art books on the subject.<ref>McCreight T. "BOOKS: Art and Design in Modern Custom Folding Knives", METALSMITH, Winter 2004, pages 18–19.</ref><ref>Mor A. "Beautiful Literature", BLAZER Magazine, August 2004, page 87 (Hebrew).</ref><ref>Guild D. "A Visual Knife Feast", BLADE, March 2005, pages 116–120.</ref><ref>Huntington R. "Art and Design in Knives", American HANDGUNNER, Jan/Feb 2007, page 78.</ref> In 2003, he published "Art and Design in Modern Custom Folding Knives",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ganoksin.com/borisat/nenam/modern-custom-folding-knives.htm|title=Book Review – Art and Design in Modern Custom Folding Knives|author=The Ganoksin Project}}</ref> and in 2005, "Art and Design in Modern Custom Fixed-Blade Knives". In 2006 he published "The Art of Modern Custom Knifemaking" and in 2007 "Modern Custom Knives – The Great Collections". Several of these volumes have been translated into 5 languages.<ref>Darom D. (2006) "Art Et Design Des Couteaux Pliants",  {{ISBN|88-6112-002-4}}.
Darom D. (2006) "Kunstvolle Messer. Handgefertigte Klappmesser aus aller Welt", White Star Verlag GmBH, {{ISBN|978-3-939128-10-6}}.
Darom D. (2006) "Arte e design dei coltelli pieghevoli", {{ISBN|88-540-0391-3}}.
Darom D. (2007) "Umeni a design sucasnosti Zakazkove Zaviraci Noze", Slovart, {{ISBN|978-80-7209-888-0}}. Дэйром Д. (2006) "НОЖИ Искусство и дизайн современных ножей", ООО "Издательство АСТ", {{ISBN|5-17-034926-2}}.
</ref>

In 2008 Darom published the first book in a new series "Custom Knifemakers of the World" with "Edmund Davidson, The Art of the Integral Knife".<ref>Jones, Clarke C. "Virginia Wildlife", April 2010, Page 7</ref><ref>"The Knife Sculptor", Roanoke Times, Sunday, 18 July 2010, Page 7</ref>
In 2009 Darom published the 2nd book in this series, "Tim Hancock, The Art of the Western Bladesmith" and a 3rd volume, "The Art Knives of Van Barnett & Dellana" was introduced in 2011.<ref>Shackleford Steve, "Window into Knifemaking", BLADE Magazine, August 2011, pages 36–38.</ref>

In October 2010, Darom was awarded the Nate Posner Memorial Award by the [[Knifemakers' Guild]] at their annual meeting in Louisville, Kentucky (USA), recognizing his "Outstanding Service in the Promotion of Handcrafted Cutlery".<ref>{{Cite web| title=Flint River Knife Club Newsletter | date=November 2010 | url=http://www.flintriverknifeclub.com/news/nov_10.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711010316/http://www.flintriverknifeclub.com/news/nov_10.pdf | archive-date=2011-07-11}}</ref>
